choices.text: Buy him off with a better prey

effects.log: You send word of a larger, stupider quarry on the far isles. It is not nice. It works.

events.text: Your guardian, {b3_beast}, is unwell. It rests at the sunny corner of the terrace all day with its great body barely stirring, ignoring the sweets and the praise. Whoever feeds it sits beside it, and your disciples take turns. A physician from another isle says it is simply age, and that nothing can be done, and does not meet your eye.

choices.text: Sit up with it through the night

effects.log: You sit up with it through the night, and say whatever comes to mind. By dawn it is breathing easier, and you are not sure which of you was being comforted.

choices.text: Go to the Nine Clouds Palace for a remedy

effects.log: You go to the Nine Clouds Palace and ask, humbly, for an elixir for a beast. The alchemists are scandalised and then charmed. The elixir works, slowly.
You ask it, plainly, what it wants. It does not answer, but at dusk it climbs, with effort, to the highest roof and watches the sun go down. You do not ask again.

events.text: A small child of the isle, someone's grandchild, has made a friend of your guardian, {b3_beast}, and is currently perched on it like a cloth on a clothes-line, singing. Their parent stands in the arch with a face that cannot decide between horror and awe. Whoever feeds it is trying not to laugh.

choices.text: Let the child stay up there

effects.log: You let the child stay up there. The guardian makes a slow tour of the whole courtyard, as if bearing an egg. The parent faints, in the end, but gently.
You gently lift the child down, and the beast sighs and settles. The child sulks for a week, and the parent sends honey cakes for a year.

choices.text: Ask the parent to bring them often

effects.log: You tell the parent to bring the child every week. The guardian is never lonelier, nor the isle safer, than in those years.

events.text: An old rival tells you, over tea and with a great show of friendliness, that your guardian, {b3_beast}, is smaller than the one their order keeps. They describe it at length. You gather that it has horns of a sort you have only read about, and a dreadful temper. Whoever feeds it is not listening, and is taking notes.

effects.log: You lay out your guardian's virtues with the zeal of a recruiting clerk. It is not necessary, and not quite dignified, and the rival is quietly impressed.

choices.text: Agree, and ask to see theirs

effects.log: You agree, warmly, and ask to see theirs. The visit is arranged, and goes oddly well; the two beasts ignore each other with great courtesy.
You change the subject to the tea, which is truly excellent. You are not drawn. The guardian, when you get home, seems pleased with you.

events.text: Your guardian, {b3_beast}, settles across the threshold every dusk, and everyone has made their peace with it. It also shreds the doormats, and no one has made their peace with that. Today the gate is full of grumbling clerks, a dozen petitions, and a guardian looking blandly at the sky.

choices.text: Fine the beast an extra sweet

effects.log: You fine the beast an extra sweet, and it accepts the punishment with resignation. The clerks leave satisfied, and the beast leaves content.

choices.text: Explain to the clerks that it is old

effects.log: You explain that it is very old, and was here before the clerks. They concede, because it is true, and because it is looking at them.
You coax it to a quieter corner with a bowl of honey-rice. It sulks for a month, then settles.

events.text: An elderly scholar from the Star Sea Pavilion has come to study your guardian, {b3_beast}, with a notebook and a hat. They ask questions with relentless courtesy: when it eats, what it fears, which stars it watches. Your guardian, at the gate, ignores them with majestic patience.

choices.text: Help the scholar with their notes

effects.log: You help the scholar with their notes, and in return learn three things about your own guardian that you never knew. One of them is moving.

choices.text: Tell them to ask the beast itself

effects.log: You tell them to ask the beast itself. After a week they come to you pale and delighted: it answered, in a way. They will not say how.

choices.text: Send them on with a polite excuse

effects.log: You send them on with a polite excuse. They go away disappointed, and publish an essay on you which is, remarkably, flattering.

events.text: Your guardian, {b3_beast}, and a neighbour's have had a stand-off at the boundary near the gate, where the two isles nearly touch. Both beasts stand with lowered heads. Both owners stand with raised voices. Between them, a fence of white cloud, which neither is willing to be first to cross.

choices.text: Settle it with a firm word

ok.log: You say a firm word, and the other owner a softer one, and the beasts back away together, each pretending it was their own idea. The cloud fence stays.

fail.log: Your word fails, and the stand-off lasts through supper and the night. By morning both beasts are asleep in the same place, and both owners are hoarse.

choices.text: Let the beasts work it out

effects.log: You let the beasts work it out. They do, with a courtesy the owners lack, and a week later they are sharing a sunny patch.
You offer to share the grazing with the neighbour. It is accepted, with a hint of triumph, and the beasts are friends for centuries.

events.text: A year of quiet with your guardian, {b3_beast}, and nothing to report but the small things: a favourite spot, a trick of the eyes, a way of lifting its head when you cross the courtyard. At the gate you find yourself speaking to it as one speaks to an old friend, and it seems, on the whole, to listen.

effects.log: You keep up the habit, and the guardian turns out to be an excellent listener with no known opinions. Your own, you notice, are clearer for it.
You teach it a new trick: to ring the temple bell on a signal. It takes a year, and the whole isle comes to watch, and it is the most useless and splendid thing you have ever done.

choices.text: Leave a gift of its favourite meal

effects.log: You leave a gift of its favourite meal, a pot of mountain honey and nine fish, and it eats the lot and falls asleep beside you.

events.text: Something wild stirs in your guardian, {b3_beast}, one spring: it stands at the gate all night, looking at the far clouds and making a low, unfamiliar sound. Your disciples keep their distance. It is clearly in some way homesick, or called, and it does not belong to you, in the end.

choices.text: Open the gate and let it go for a season

effects.log: You open the gate and let it go for a season. It returns after a hundred days, gaunt and content, and settles as if it had never left.

choices.text: Keep the gate shut, and stay near

effects.log: You keep the gate shut, and stay near, talking until the mood passes. It does, eventually, but something has shifted between you.

choices.text: Walk out with it into the night

effects.log: You walk out with it into the night, the two of you, as far as the edge of the isle. It stops. It looks at you. It turns back.

effects.log: You turn back, steering by the stars. {b3_pet} sulks the whole way, and then, near home, forgives you, with a long call.

choices.text: Land and make a camp for the night

effects.log: You land and make a camp. {b3_pet} stands guard through the dark, a pale, patient shape, and you sleep better than in years.

events.text: A visitor to your isle, someone of rank, is greeted by {b3_pet}, which leaves for three days and returns with a feather that is not its own. The visitor's party gasps. {b3_pet} regards them with its usual secretive air. You can feel the weight of the Court's etiquette descending on the scene like a damp cloak.

choices.text: Smooth it over with a joke

ok.log: You smooth it over with a joke, and the visitor, to everyone's relief, laughs. They ask, a little wistfully, whether {b3_pet} is for sale. It is not.

fail.log: The joke lands badly, and the visitor leaves with a frozen smile. {b3_pet}, in the garden, looks pleased with itself.

effects.log: You apologise gravely, in the full form of the Court. The visitor is charmed by the effort, if not by {b3_pet}.
You blame {b3_pet}, openly and with a straight face. The visitor decides you are a person of humour, and sends a gift of grain.

events.text: {b3_pet} has dropped a feather at your door, long and silver-white, still warm. In the sea-cloud country this is a token of trust, the sort of thing a crane gives once or twice in a century. {b3_pet}, a restless crane, forever at the edge of the isle, is the last creature you expected to be so tender. It watches to see what you do.

effects.log: You wear it in your hair for a year, and it stays bright. People assume it is a rank. It is better than a rank.
You press it in a book, between two pages you have always meant to read. Decades on, you find it, and it is still faintly warm.

choices.text: Give one of your own in return

effects.log: You give one of your own hairs in return, bound with a thread. {b3_pet} holds it a long time in its beak, and then flies off with it, and it is a long time before you see it.

events.text: A storm comes up from the sea of clouds without warning, and {b3_pet} is not home. You wait on the terrace, wind pulling at your sleeves, while the horizon goes the colour of a bruise. {b3_pet} is a restless crane, forever at the edge of the isle, and this, you remind yourself, is exactly the sort of weather it likes.

choices.text: Go out and look for it

effects.log: You go out and look for it, in the storm, and find it riding a gust with its wings wide and its eyes shut, quite happy. You are soaked. It is not.

choices.text: Light a lamp on the terrace

effects.log: You light a lamp on the terrace and keep it burning through the night. At dawn {b3_pet} lands beside it, damp and ordinary, and eats your breakfast.

choices.text: Call it with the old whistle

effects.log: You call it with the old whistle. It appears out of the dark within a minute, offended at the interruption, and lands on your head.
